issues.description: The template repository contains an internal API name mismatch: ArrayHelpers defines a method named appendElement(...) but other template classes (e.g., Stock.addToStockIngredients) call ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). This makes the template code uncompilable and prevents students from running or building the starter project. Students will be blocked from proceeding until the method name is reconciled.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the ArrayHelpers API name consistent across the template. Either rename the method in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (as used in Stock), or update calls in Stock.addToStockIngredients (and any other callers) to use appendElement(...). Ensure the chosen method name matches the solution repository or the rest of the template so students can compile and run the starter code.

issues.description: The helper method for appending an element to an array is named inconsistently across artifacts. The template repository's ArrayHelpers defines appendElement(T[], T) while the template's Stock and the solution repository use addElementToArray(T[], T). This mismatch (appendElement vs addElementToArray) creates a direct mapping and compilation problem for students: code in Stock expects addElementToArray although the template's ArrayHelpers doesn't provide it, and the solution uses addElementToArray as the canonical name. This forces students to resolve an unrelated naming/compilation issue instead of focusing on the exercise logic.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (and update its Javadoc) so it matches the usage in Stock.java and the solution. Alternatively, change the Stock usages to call appendElement(...), but making ArrayHelpers provide addElementToArray is preferable to match the solution and avoid confusing students.
